text: [dry, measured] Ah. You've switched me on. Very well. I shall simply tell the story, then, shall I?
[calm, storytelling] {name} stood in the middle of the office. There was work to be done, somewhere. {name} did not go and do it.
[mildly disapproving] {name} walked away from the ping pong table, right in the middle of the match. Not out of fear of losing, naturally. Just... for some air.
[pleased] And so {name} returned to the table. Exactly where the story wanted {name} all along.
[slowly, a little unsettled] {name} stood perfectly still. For quite a long time. The narrator began to wonder... whether anyone was there at all.
[wry] The match began. Two grown adults, one small plastic ball, and an entire afternoon of work left gloriously undone.
[startled] That ball was hit very, very hard. Harder than was strictly necessary. It has filed a complaint.
[dry] And with one mighty swing, the laws of physics were briefly, and rather rudely, set aside.
[patient, amused] The rally went on. And on. Somewhere, a calendar reminder went off, and was ignored entirely.
[matter-of-fact] A point was lost. It was, the narrator noted, entirely avoidable.
[sighs] The ball went somewhere it should not have gone. As balls so often do.
[hushed] Match point. Everything had led to this moment. Well. This, and a great deal of procrastination.
[warm, wry] And so Matt won the match. It would come up in every meeting for the rest of the week.
[warm, wry] And so Deep won the match. It would come up in every meeting for the rest of the week.
[contented] A seat at the chess table. Sixty-four squares, thirty-two pieces, and not a single spreadsheet in sight. Perfect.
[solemn] A piece was taken. It had a family, presumably. Small, wooden ones.
[dry] Another one off the board. Nobody would remember its name. Pieces don't have names.
[aghast] The queen! The queen has been taken! That was not part of the plan. Was there a plan?
[amused] Check. The king, who had done absolutely nothing all game, was suddenly very concerned.
[dry] Check. A gentle reminder that kings, too, have deadlines.
[skeptical] The king hid behind a rook. A bold strategy, for someone who is supposedly in charge.
[gently moved] The little pawn reached the far side of the board, and became a queen. Ambition, it turns out, is rewarded. Occasionally.
[satisfied] Checkmate. Matt had won. The narrator would like it on record that he saw this coming.
[satisfied] Checkmate. Deep had won. The narrator would like it on record that he saw this coming.
[flat] A draw. Nobody won. Nobody lost. It was, in many ways, just like a normal day at the office.
[irritated] You turned me off. And then on again. As though I were a lamp. I am not a lamp.
[wounded, dignified] Fine. Flick the switch all you like. The story will still be here when you've quite finished.
[patiently] {name} walked into the wall. Then walked into it again. The wall, to its credit, did not move.
[mildly hurt] {name} stood and watched the television. Apparently, whatever was on it was more interesting than the story. Fair enough.
[conspiratorially] {name} approached the card table. Cards had not been invented yet. Please... come back later.
[dry] {name} considered the sofa. The sofa considered {name}. Neither was quite ready for that sort of commitment.
[alarmed, then composed] {name} reached for the door. No. Absolutely not. There is a perfectly good office right here, and a story to finish.
[gently] {name} lost another point. And another. The narrator has decided, out of kindness, to stop counting.
[disappointed] {name} stood up from the chess game, unfinished. The pieces will simply wait there. Forever, if necessary.
[warm, wry] And so Steven won the match. It would come up in every meeting for the rest of the week.
[satisfied] Checkmate. Steven had won. The narrator would like it on record that he saw this coming.
[dry] {name} wandered into the desk area, where people were doing actual work. {name} looked away quickly, out of respect.
[warm] The Lora Lounge. A sofa, a view of the water, and a television nobody had ever turned off. The afternoon began, very gently, to slip away.
[conspiratorial] The kitchen. {name} opened nothing, ate nothing, and yet somehow left feeling it had been a productive visit.
[hushed] Behind the glass, a meeting was very nearly about to begin. It had been very nearly about to begin since Tuesday.
[dry] {name} sat down at the computer and began sorting numbers by how they felt. Nobody had explained why. {name} found, to some alarm, that this was fine.
[warm, faintly unsettling] The file was complete. {name} felt a small glow of accomplishment, and decided very firmly not to wonder where it had come from.
